free.subject: Your 10 Claude Skills (2-minute setup)
free.html:
Hey, Levi here. Thanks for grabbing the Starter Vault.

Quick setup so you actually use it today:

1. Unzip the download.
2. In Claude go to Settings → Capabilities → Skills and upload the zip (or the folder you want).
3. Ask for a task in plain words, like "reply to this email: …". Claude picks the skill by itself.

Start with Skill Maker. Describe one task you repeat every week and let it write your first own skill.

Reply and tell me which task eats most of your week. I read every reply.

Levi

free.subject: The #1 reason a Claude Skill doesn't fire
free.html:
Most skills that "don't work" have the same problem: the description is a label, not a trigger.

Bad: Helps with marketing.
Good: Use when the user asks for hooks, opening lines or first sentences for a post, or says their posts get no reach.

Claude matches the situation and the words people actually say. Write those into the description and the skill loads every time.

Open any skill from the vault and look at its description. That's the pattern to copy.

Levi

free.subject: What a full pack looks like (Content Engine)
free.html:
The free vault covers general work. The packs go deep on one job.

Example, Content Engine (12 skills): voice profile → hook writer → X thread builder → LinkedIn posts → Threads batch → repurpose anything → 30-day calendar → carousel → reply writer → post audit → bio optimizer.

The voice profile is the piece people tell me they didn't know they needed. Every other writing skill reads it first, so the output stops sounding like AI.

There are 9 packs like this: content, email, sales pages, cold outreach, SEO, digital products, faceless video, Claude Code for non-coders, and Claude + n8n.

pack.subject: Get more out of your skill pack
pack.html:
Thanks for buying, Levi here.

One tip that doubles the quality of every skill in your pack: paste one great past example of the result inside the skill file and add the line "match this quality and length".

A skill without an example is a guess. With one, it copies your standard.
